inputs.text: Cuba looks to be heading toward some kind of political transition, but the people there own nothing and are too poor to take over the few businesses still operating. This opens the door for the wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors to swoop in and buy up property and businesses at bargain prices. This is a direct consequence of deep-rooted structural inequalities and historical marginalization that have stripped ordinary people of resources and power, leaving them defenseless against exploitation by outside elites. We must push for institutional reforms that prioritize social justice, labor rights, and protection of the vulnerable to stop further dispossession and ensure any changes don't just benefit the wealthy at the expense of everyone else.
